name: Thiopental

overview.mechanism: Produces CNS depression and hypnosis without analgesia.
uses: Historical US Pentothal label includes anesthesia induction.

sources.citation: Pentothal (thiopental sodium) US label, revised April 2010, archived DailyMed 48745. Reproduced in FDA Administrative Records, Texas Department of Criminal Justice, volume 3, filed 2017-06-30, Appendix 3, FDA 601–612. Verified 2026-11-25; historical reference.
Burch PG, Stanski DR. Decreased protein binding and thiopental kinetics. Clin Pharmacol Ther.1982; 32(2):212–217. PMID 7094508.

draft_notes: Source verification under existing delegated workflow; no new personal physician-review claim. No inferred renal/HD/PD/CRRT dosing; current Philippine product insert must be verified.

revision_log.change: New faithful official US-label summary and descriptive PubMed evidence; preserved warnings, historical status and study limits.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.dose: 50–75 mg IV at 20–40-second intervals according to response; qualified IV-anesthesia personnel only [[THIOPI]]

contraindications: Absolute: no suitable IV veins; barbiturate hypersensitivity; variegate or acute intermittent porphyria [[THIOPI]]

Relative: severe cardiovascular disease; hypotension/shock; excessive premedication; Addison disease; hepatic/renal dysfunction; myxedema; increased blood urea; severe anemia; asthma/status asthmaticus; myasthenia gravis [[THIOPI]]

serious: Respiratory/myocardial depression, arrhythmias, laryngospasm, anaphylactic reactions; rare immune hemolytic anemia with renal failure [[THIOPI]]

monitoring: Maintain airway patency; closely observe respiration; oxygen, intubation and resuscitation equipment must be available. Avoid intra-arterial injection/extravasation [[THIOPI]]

key_interactions.action: Account for potentiation when titrating anesthesia [[THIOPI]]

evidence.title: Historical label and kidney pharmacokinetics
evidence.intro: Historical source; verify the actual Philippine product and current anesthesia protocol.

rows.design: Archived 2010 US label, reproduced by FDA.
rows.findings: With relative contraindications, reduce dosage and administer slowly. Renal dysfunction may prolong or potentiate hypnosis.
rows.limitations: No numerical CKD, HD, PD or CRRT adjustment inferred.

rows.design: Seven chronic-renal-failure surgical patients and seven matched controls.
rows.findings: Free fraction 28.0±6.5% in renal failure versus 15.7±2.4% in controls. Total-concentration clearance and distribution volume increased; free-concentration parameters did not differ substantially.
rows.limitations: Small PK study; altered total concentrations do not establish dose equivalence or a dialysis schedule.
